summary: The design reuses valuable dev-loop pieces, but several proposed contracts do not match their current APIs. The review focused on isolation/retry semantics, MCP job lifecycle, deterministic scheduling, prompt/profile wiring, and telemetry fidelity.

suggestions.title: Introduce task-attempt worktree primitives
suggestions.rationale: `DevAgentPool` retries using the same `cwd`, while `SubWorktreeManager` is keyed by worker id and creates a fixed branch/path. That cannot guarantee C4’s fresh sub-worktree on attempt 2 or support per-task `coder_merge` results without a new task/attempt-oriented lifecycle API.

suggestions.title: Add reservation, idempotency, and crash recovery
suggestions.rationale: `TaskScheduler` treats every non-`done` task as pending, while the stdio server keeps execution state only in process memory. Repeated `coder_plan`/`coder_run_chunk` calls or a server restart can duplicate work, orphan branches, or lose job status; task/job identity must be persisted or deterministically reconciled from git.

suggestions.title: Make wave ordering stable before rotating roster seats
suggestions.rationale: `TaskScheduler.next_wave()` iterates a set and explicitly promises no ordering. Chunk assignment and rotating model starts will therefore vary across processes, undermining reproducibility and telemetry comparisons; preserve index order or define a stable task-id tie-breaker and test it.

suggestions.title: Make long-running MCP calls background jobs at the transport boundary
suggestions.rationale: `StdioMCPServer.start()` awaits each request inline, and `handle_tools_call()` awaits the tool body. A `coder_run_chunk` implementation that merely creates an internal job after doing setup still blocks the MCP request; it must schedule work immediately, return a Pydantic job envelope, and allow `status`/`wait` requests to be processed concurrently.

suggestions.title: Reject dirty or untracked coder worktrees before merge
suggestions.rationale: The proposed fidelity check relies on committed `git diff`, but the existing manager only checks branch commits and can merge a branch while leaving untracked or uncommitted coder changes behind. Native Haiku has no dispatcher output validation, so `coder_merge` should require a clean status, verify commit-only code changes against the task allowlist, and reject SDD changes before merging.

suggestions.title: Use explicit Pydantic argument and result models for every coder tool
suggestions.rationale: The generic MCP adapter calls `tool._execute()` directly, so generated schemas do not enforce arguments by themselves. `OptimizationToolkitBase` demonstrates the required `_pre_execute` validation and JSON-safe `ToolResult` shaping; the coder toolkit should follow that pattern for job ids, snapshots, outcomes, diagnostics, and path constraints.

suggestions.title: Separate roster seats from the existing dev-loop pool spec
suggestions.rationale: `DevAgentSpec` models same-backend `escalation_model` retries, whereas this feature needs cross-backend roster rotation, native seats, and a fixed `sdd-coder` subagent. Existing profiles default to `sdd-worker`, and `DevAgentBackend` lacks `google-compat`; overloading these types risks silently dispatching the old state-mutating prompt or applying the wrong retry policy.

suggestions.title: Define a first-class per-attempt telemetry record
suggestions.rationale: `DispatchLabels` carries task/model/attempt, but `WaveResult` and `WorkerSummary` do not carry duration, token usage, backend outcome, retry diagnostics, or native-agent evidence. `LLMCodeDispatcher` publishes usage to events rather than returning it, so Completion Notes cannot reliably meet the requested telemetry contract without an explicit aggregation model.

suggestions.title: Add a Gemini tool-call wire-format regression test
suggestions.rationale: The current `_tool_call_to_openai_dict()` drops all provider-specific fields, exactly where Gemini `thought_signature` would be lost. Test a multi-turn assistant/tool exchange with synthetic raw tool calls, assert the signature is echoed only for the Gemini override, and verify ordinary OpenAI-compatible calls remain unchanged.

suggestions.title: Test native Haiku through the same merge contract
suggestions.rationale: The existing dispatcher tests validate `DevelopmentOutput`, but the native Claude Code path returns a final message plus git state and bypasses that validation. Add tests that cover prepared branch creation, native completion, clean/dirty status, fidelity violations, merge conflicts, and the third Sonnet attempt without trusting the agent’s prose.

suggestions.title: Move synchronous index reads off the async MCP path
suggestions.rationale: `TaskScheduler.from_index_file()` uses synchronous `Path.read_text()`. Calling it directly from async `coder_plan` violates the repository’s async-I/O rule and can block the stdio server while reading a large or slow filesystem; use an async boundary such as `asyncio.to_thread()` or an async scheduler reader.

suggestions.title: Wire probe and client cleanup to actual server lifecycle
suggestions.rationale: `AbstractToolkit.auto_open` runs only on the first tool call, while `create_toolkit_mcp_server()` registers the toolkit and `StdioMCPServer.start()` never invokes toolkit `start`/`stop` hooks. A startup roster probe therefore will not happen at startup, and provider clients/background jobs may not be closed deterministically unless the server owns explicit lifecycle callbacks.
